methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $305M total raised proxy.

private.name: ICON
private.rationale: Same sector (Housing & Construction), same stage (Series C)

data.narrative:
Meter is a Series C-stage company in Housing & Construction that has raised $304.9M to date. The comparable universe for this valuation is limited: one identified private peer (ICON) and no public housing-construction technology comps, reflecting the nascent nature of frontier construction tech.

Given the sparse comp availability, this analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total raised ($305M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series C-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.7x yields an implied valuation of $518M. This single-method approach generates a triangulated range from $441M (low) to $596M (high), with $518M as the median point. The low and high bounds reflect reasonable ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result in the absence of multiple independent valuation anchors.

Key uncertainties materially constrain confidence in this range. The single-method foundation leaves no cross-validation from revenue multiples, discounted cash flow, or market comparables—standard triangulation tools inapplicable due to data unavailability. The private comp set (one peer) is too thin to support meaningful relative valuation. Series C step-up multipliers vary substantially by market conditions, capital availability, and company-specific trajectory. Without visibility into Meter's unit economics, growth rate, or capital efficiency relative to peers, the $441M–$596M range should be treated as indicative rather than definitive. Additional data on revenue scale or profitability pathway would materially sharpen this valuation.
